_meta.description: Synthetic NVDA earnings call transcript — Q3 FY2025 (Oct 2024). Exercises: guidance extraction, sentiment, evasiveness detection.

transcript:
OPERATOR: Welcome to NVIDIA's third quarter fiscal 2025 earnings call. I will now turn the call over to Jen Jensen Huang, CEO.

JENSEN HUANG: Thank you. Good afternoon, everyone. We delivered another record quarter with revenue of $35.1 billion, up 94% year over year and up 17% sequentially. Data Center revenue was $30.8 billion, up 112% year over year. Our Hopper architecture remains in high demand. Blackwell production is ramping and shipments have begun. We expect Blackwell revenue in the billions in Q4.

Operating income was $21.9 billion, a 66% operating margin. We generated $17.6 billion in free cash flow. We returned $11.2 billion to shareholders through buybacks and dividends.

Looking ahead, for Q4 fiscal 2025 we expect revenue of $37.5 billion, plus or minus 2%. GAAP gross margins of approximately 73%, down from 74.6% this quarter due to Blackwell ramp costs. Operating expenses of approximately $3.3 billion GAAP.

The AI infrastructure buildout is accelerating. Every major cloud provider is expanding capacity. We see sovereign AI demand growing. Automotive is now over $300 million quarterly run rate.

OPERATOR: We will now take questions. First caller.

ANALYST 1 (Morgan Stanley): Jensen, can you talk about Blackwell supply constraints and when they ease?

JENSEN HUANG: Blackwell demand is extraordinary. I believe we will be supply constrained well into next year. Our supply chain partners are doing everything they can. We are working closely with TSMC and our memory partners. The ramp is progressing well.

ANALYST 2 (Goldman Sachs): What's your visibility into China export controls and the impact?

JENSEN HUANG: Export controls are always a variable we operate within. We have compliant products for all markets. We continue to serve China with H20 and other compliant products. The situation evolves and we monitor it carefully. I'm not going to give you a specific revenue number for China.

ANALYST 3 (UBS): Gross margins dipped. Is 73% the trough for Blackwell ramp?

COLETTE KRESS (CFO): We expect margins to recover in the first half of fiscal 2026 as Blackwell yields improve and mix normalizes. We are comfortable with our long-term gross margin target in the mid-70s.

ANALYST 4 (Bernstein): Are you seeing any order cancellations or pushouts from hyperscalers?

JENSEN HUANG: Demand remains exceptionally strong. We haven't seen cancellations. There are always scheduling adjustments in a ramp of this complexity, but nothing that concerns us. Our customers are signaling continued investment acceleration.
